severity: ROOT CAUSE of 'the policy never presses the plunger' -- the reward never asked it to
claim: The scene's `object` is not a passive cylinder: it is an IsaacLab Articulation whose prismatic `PistonJoint` IS the pipette plunger. The v1 reward reads only rigid-body positions (body_pos_w) and never reads joint_pos, so depressing the plunger -- the functional act the task is named for -- was never measured, never rewarded, and never required for 'success'.
discovery: Found by direct scene enumeration after a visual observation that the policy 'is not pressing the plunger'. The observation was correct and the metric was blind to it.

scene_facts.Rod: the PLUNGER; also the articulation ROOT link (the part the robot grasps)
scene_facts.Barrel: the pipette body; the rod slides through its bore
scene_facts.drive: passive spring+damper with rest target 0.0 -- returns to rest when released

what_v1_scored: reach, grasp, lift, tube-proximity, plate-proximity, settle -- all from positions. v1 'success' = pipette carried over the pot and settled. Neither insertion nor plunger actuation is tested. Consistent with the manifest: every screened demonstration scores success:True with tube:False.
consequence_for_rl: The RL policies optimised exactly what was scored. A reward with no plunger term provides no gradient toward pressing the plunger, so the absence of pressing in the learned policy is expected behaviour, not a training failure.
validity_of_prior_results: All v1 numbers remain valid UNDER THE V1 PREDICATE (transport-based). v1 is frozen, not edited, so every prior claim stays reproducible; v2 is a separate module and every rollout can be scored under both.
fix: rlinf/envs/isaaclab/tasks/g1_piston_reward_v2.py: adds press (plunger > 50% travel while held) and dispense (press while aligned over the tube) stages, tightens the tube stage to a real insertion tolerance with a height gate, and closes the v1 lift exploit with a ballistic-speed test. Plunger shaping is best-so-far so the spring-loaded joint cannot be pumped for reward (pinned by test_pumping_the_spring_loaded_plunger_cannot_farm_reward).

demonstration_measurement.method: All recorded demonstrations replayed through the frozen mapper+retargeter while logging PistonJoint position and Rod-Barrel separation.
demonstration_measurement.result: SPLIT. 3 of 9 measured episodes (10, 15, 45) depress the plunger past 50% of travel (55-60%); the rest reach only 22-30%, consistent with passive spring compression from gripping. Rod-Barrel separation corroborates: pressing episodes compress to 6-8 mm, non-pressing stay at 18-21 mm.
demonstration_measurement.mechanism: The pressing and non-pressing demonstrations issue nearly IDENTICAL hand commands (same thumb/finger ranges and maxima) and near-identical arm trajectories (mean difference 0.02-0.05 rad). The press is therefore CONTACT-SENSITIVE rather than a distinct commanded motion: whether the plunger goes down depends on exactly how the hand closes on it, not on a separate "press" action in the demonstration.
demonstration_measurement.implication_for_rl: Two consequences. (1) RLPD demo replay does contain pressing, but at ~1/3 density, so it is a weak prior. (2) Because the press is contact-sensitive, an explicit reward term is the right instrument: the policy cannot copy a "press action" from the data, it has to discover the grip geometry that produces compression -- which is exactly what a reward on measured plunger depth optimises.

CORRECTION_2026_08_31.what_was_claimed: An earlier reading of this measurement said '3 of 11 demonstrations press the plunger past 50% of travel, so the behaviour exists in the data at low density and RLPD demo replay supplies a weak prior for it.'
CORRECTION_2026_08_31.why_it_was_wrong: The 11 replayed act_ep*.npy files are a SPREAD sampled across all 67 dataset episodes, not the RLPD demo buffer. Only 3 of those 11 (eps 0, 5, 40) are in the 22 executable episodes the buffer actually holds. The sample was unrepresentative of what RLPD trains on.
CORRECTION_2026_08_31.corrected_finding: The three episodes that press deepest (10: 59%, 15: 60%, 45: 55%) are ALL NON-EXECUTABLE -- they fail to lift the pipette at all (2 stages, return ~2.97). The three EXECUTABLE episodes press only 26%, 46% and 27%. Plunger depth ANTI-correlates with lifting (corr -0.350; mean press 30% when lifted vs 41% when not).
CORRECTION_2026_08_31.mechanism: Deep plunger compression in this data is a SYMPTOM OF FAILURE, not of dispensing: when the grasp does not close correctly the fingers crush the plunger down while the pipette stays socketed. A successful pick shows LESS compression, because the hand lifts the object rather than pressing it into its holder.
CORRECTION_2026_08_31.implication: No demonstration in the executable set performs a deliberate dispense. RLPD demo replay therefore supplies NO prior for the functional act -- it must be discovered from reward alone. It also means a naive 'reward deep plunger travel' term would reward the failure mode, which is why the v3 press stage additionally requires a LIVE grasp and the dispense stage requires being aligned over the tube while holding it.
